title: Ask
body: Answers questions and researches your codebase without changing anything.
useWhen: you want to understand code, compare approaches or check an idea before touching files.
example: #selection Why does this hook re-render on every keystroke? Answer in under 5 lines.

title: Plan
body: Researches the task and writes an implementation plan for you to review before any code changes. You can also start it with /plan.
useWhen: the change touches more than one or two files, or you are not sure of the approach yet.
example: /plan Add rate limiting to the public API routes. List the files you would change and the risks. No code yet.

title: Agent
body: Implements changes: edits files, runs commands and checks the result. The most capable role and the most expensive, because every file read and tool run adds tokens.
useWhen: you know what you want, the plan is agreed and you can name the files and how to check it worked.
example: Implement step 1 of the plan only. Run npm test afterwards and show me the summary line.

title: Edit (deprecated)
body: Edit mode is deprecated and hidden by default. Use Agent for multi-file edits. If you really need it back, set chat.editMode.hidden to false.
useWhen: you are following an older guide that mentions it. Translate “Edit mode” to Agent.
